native_result.query: In which millenium did amber had the highest value and in what time interval did it peak?
native_result.HypoA: Amber has historically high and stable values in the 4th millenium BCE. with its all time peak around 3300 to 3000BCE.
native_result.HypoB: El ambar alcanza su valor maximo durante el IV milenio BCE (4000-3001 BCE; ~5950-5001 calBP), dentro de una meseta de maximo que se extiende entre 4000 y 3000 BCE (~5950-4851 calBP, definida como los bins seculares contiguos con Z >= 0.9*maximo: 11 bins, Z medio 1.489), con el pico estricto en 3300-3000 BCE (~5250-4851 calBP, Z = 1.54). Los Z son indices estandarizados de visibilidad/intensidad arqueologica, no valor economico directo: la hipotesis es que la mayor visibilidad del ambar en el IV milenio BCE refleja su mayor valor relativo (demanda, circulacion y/o deposito). La meseta arranca en el Neolitico medio/bajo (EN, 4000-3500 BCE, Z=1.46) y culmina en el Neolitico medio final (MN, 3400-3000 BCE, Z=1.54) justo en la frontera EN/MN; despues cae a valores negativos desde el III milenio BCE (media -0.148) hasta minimos en el I milenio BCE (-0.727). El pico excede lo predecible por la intensidad de registro global (Ambar IV = +1.484 vs kde estandarizado +0.908, delta +0.576), pero corr(Ambar, kde_all_mean)=0.626 y la meseta cae en el percentil 78 del kde, por lo que no se descarta una contribucion parcial del sesgo de muestreo. Limites: resolucion real de bins de 100 anos, y el bin 3000 BCE es ambiguo entre IV y III milenio segun la convencion de frontera (elegida: floor((BCE-1)/1000)+1, resuelta a favor del IV por la media y por 3 de los 4 bins empatados en el maximo).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Validacion de insumos y merge capital.csv (decimal=',') con time_series_data.csv sobre CE=-BCE: 37 bins coincidentes, max|Zamber-Amber|=0.0. 2) Serie primaria = 37 bins seculares crudos (Amber); comprobado que Amber_inter es interpolacion lineal determinista (np.allclose vs np.interp) y usada solo como control (reproduce el argmax). 3) Asignacion de milenio BCE (floor((BCE-1)/1000)+1) y Z por milenio por media y por maximo. 4) Argmax estricto + rachas contiguas sobre tres umbrales (0.9*max, media+1sd, mediana+IQR) mas suplente mediana+0.5*IQR. 5) Sensibilidad con los 39 bins de capital.csv. 6) Chequeo de confuso con kde_all_mean por bin y por milenio. 7) Contexto cultural con la columna group de capital.csv. 8) Tablas guardadas en outputs/.

sub_hypo.context: Primary analysis uses 37 matched raw 100-year bins from capital.csv and time_series_data.csv, merged on CE = -BCE; Zamber and Amber agree exactly. sub_hypo.relations: Amber Z has its highest millennium-level mean in the fourth millennium BCE (+1.484). Higher standardized archaeological visibility/intensity is hypothesized to indicate greater relative value, not direct economic value.

sub_hypo.text: Amber's maximum plateau extends from 4000 to 3000 BCE (approximately 5950–4851 calBP), with a strict peak at 3300–3000 BCE (approximately 5250–4851 calBP).
sub_hypo.context: Raw 100-year bins; the maximum plateau is defined by contiguous bins with Z >= 0.9 times the maximum. The workflow also checks runs using mean + 1 SD, median + IQR, and median + 0.5 IQR thresholds.
sub_hypo.relations: Eleven contiguous bins meet the maximum-plateau threshold, averaging Z = 1.489. Four bins at 3300–3000 BCE tie for the strict maximum, Z = 1.54.

sub_hypo.text: The amber plateau starts in the middle/lower Neolithic (EN, 4000–3500 BCE) and culminates in the final middle Neolithic (MN, 3400–3000 BCE), at the EN/MN boundary, before declining in subsequent millennia.
sub_hypo.context: Cultural periods are identified using capital.csv's group column; temporal comparisons use raw 100-year bins and millennium summaries.
sub_hypo.relations: Amber Z rises from 1.46 in EN to 1.54 in MN, then becomes negative from the third millennium BCE (mean -0.148), reaching minima in the first millennium BCE (-0.727).

sub_hypo.text: The fourth-millennium amber peak exceeds what global recording intensity predicts, although a partial contribution from sampling bias cannot be excluded.
sub_hypo.context: Amber and kde_all_mean are compared by matched 100-year bin and by millennium, including the fourth-millennium peak and the 4000–3000 BCE plateau.
sub_hypo.relations: Fourth-millennium Amber is +1.484 versus standardized KDE +0.908, a difference of +0.576. Amber and kde_all_mean are positively correlated (r = 0.626), and the plateau lies at the 78th percentile of KDE, leaving possible partial sampling confounding.
